title: Living with Lp(a)
summary:
Background: Some children have an inherited high level of a particular blood-fat protein from birth. This level can hardly be influenced and may later increase the risk of heart and circulatory disease. For children, there is currently no effective treatment for it. Many families find this news distressing and worry about their child's future. So far, little is known about how much children and their parents are emotionally affected by it.

Research question: We want to find out how burdened parents and children are in this situation, whether parents and children experience the burden differently, and which circumstances (for example knowledge about the condition or uncertainty) are related to it. We are also interested in how well-being develops over the course of one year.

Methods: Families with an affected child (aged 8 to 17 years) and one parent each take part. At three time points within one year, parents and children complete short questionnaires about worries, well-being and their experience. The first is completed in the clinic, the other two conveniently from home. In addition, information already available from routine care is used. No additional examinations or blood samples are taken, and no treatment is changed.
conditions: Isolated elevation of lipoprotein(a) in childhood and adolescence (elevated lipoprotein(a) with normal LDL cholesterol, without effective drug therapy in childhood). The study investigates the associated psychosocial burden – in particular anxiety symptoms and well-being – in affected children/adolescents and their parents.

interventions.name: Non-interventional cohort of families with one child (aged 8–17 years) with isolated Lp(a) elevation and one participating parent. No intervention is administered; questionnaire data and routine clinical data (Lp(a), LDL cholesterol, anthropometrics) are collected at three time points over 12 months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents aged 8–17 years with isolated Lp(a) elevation (Lp(a) >75 nmol/l or approx. >30 mg/dl with LDL cholesterol <130 mg/dl); including index child and siblings if they also show Lp(a) elevation
one participating parent/legal guardian per family
sufficient German language skills of the child and at least one parent
written informed consent of the legal guardian(s) (both in case of joint custody) and age-appropriate assent of the child
Exclusion criteria:
acute psychiatric crisis or manifest psychiatric disorder precluding participation (based on clinical judgement)
severe cognitive impairment precluding completion of questionnaires
lack of reachability for follow-up assessments (no e-mail access, no telephone number)
current statin therapy
